results.title: Buying and caring for your puppy
results.creator_credit: Harry Cooper, Kevin Manning, Hero Productions and Visual Entertainment Group
results.brief_description: Buying a puppy takes a lot of time and consideration. Dr Harry Cooper tries to assist this process by providing the viewer with a broad overview of over twenty breeds and cross breeds, and examining the merits of how to select the right breed of dog to suit you. Factors taken into consideration include health, lifestyle and budget. Once a breed has been selected, Dr Harry goes through ensuring you choose a healthy pup, settling the pup in, training, socialisation, feeding, general health and grooming. Dr Harry Cooper has been a practicing veterinary surgeon for over thirty years and has practiced in Sydney, Tasmania and England. Over this time he has bred a wide variety of dogs including Bulldogs, Whippets, Cavalier King Charles, Dobermans, Border Collies and Mini Foxies.

results.title: Buy now, die later: the impact of television advertising on children's diets: a media debate
results.creator_credit: John Moss and Video Education Australasia
results.brief_description: ‘Buy now, die later’ proposes startling questions about children, advertising and diet. Questions such as why food advertising dominates children’s programs, why some foodstuffs receive more promotion than others, the issue of self-regulation, and most importantly, whether there is evidence of a negative impact on children’s health attributed to advertising. John Schwartz, a dietician from the Media Department of Swinburne University as well as Deputy Director of the Australian Food Council and a spokesperson for Youth Media Australia, analyses food ads to determine their effectiveness. An activities and discussion sheet accompanies the video.

results.title: Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid (Captioned)
results.creator_credit: George Roy Hill, John Foreman and Twentieth Century-Fox Film Corporation
results.brief_description: Prime western with warmth and great humour about the exploits of one of the last great bands of outlaws since Jesse James. Butch Cassidy and the deadly Sundance Kid are the most likeable outlaws in the West and amongst the most successful until their most ingenious caper, a round-trip train robbery, backfires, putting the west’s most relentless bounty hunters on their trail. Butch and the Kid use all their wiles to avoid capture, and finally elude their posse by making a hair-raising hundred foot jump into a raging mountain stream. Headed for Bolivia, the outlaws continue to rob banks until they meet their destiny. Stars Paul Newman, Robert Redford and Katharine Ross.

results.title: Buster Keaton rides again
results.creator_credit: John Spotton, Julian Biggs and National Film Board of Canada
results.brief_description: In this film Buster Keaton rides across Canada on a railway scooter and, between times, rests in a specially appointed passenger coach where he and Mrs Keaton lived during their Canadian film assignment. This film is about how Buster Keaton made a Canadian travel film, “The Railrodder”. In this informal study the comedian regales the film crew with anecdotes of a lifetime in show business. Excerpts from his silent slapstick films are shown. Awards: Seven, including Venice; New York; Melbourne; Milan. Commentary by Donald Brittain.

results.title: Buster Keaton : a hard act to follow
results.brief_description: Buster Keaton is now regarded as one of the supreme comedians of the silent American cinema. He was also an inventive and dedicated film-maker who performed all of his own stunts yet took little interest in business arrangements. This is a comprehensive survey of Buster Keaton’s life and work including generous extracts from all his feature films and most of his two-reelers. Narrated by Lindsay Anderson. Ep. 1. (53 min.)—Ep. 2. (54 min.)—Ep. 3. (53 min.) Further reference: http://www.busterkeaton.com

results.title: Business: what's it all about?
results.brief_description: This film presents the operations of four different companies relating to basic business functions, problems, skills needed and the importance of business in everyday life. Shows that certain concepts are common to any business such as profit, the distinction between products and services, research and development, production and manufacturing marketing and distribution. Suitable for upper secondary level.

results.title: Bushfire moon
results.brief_description: It’s the week before Christmas, 1891. The Australian bush is tinder dry as a fierce drought brings an infant nation to its knees. When eight year old Ned O’Day mistakes a roguish ex-miner for Father Christmas, Ned’s firm belief and sense of wonder bring about a startling turn of events. Stars John Waters and Dee Wallace.

results.title: Bush pilot: reflections on a Canadian myth
results.creator_credit: Bob Lower, Norma Bailey, Jerry Krepakevich, Michael Scott and National Film Board of Canada
results.brief_description: For some bush pilots, flying is like playing solo violin at Carnegie Hall. For others, it’s like driving a taxi. This film shows how bush pilots are slowly being replaced. In northern towns built by bulldozers and jet aircraft, the emphasis is not on adapting to the north, but on remaking it in the image of the south. This is a thought provoking film about northern development.
